vulns.title: settle_fee bounds only the fee magnitude, not its sign, so a caller-supplied negative fee inflates their collateral
vulns.root_cause: The integrator/trading fee is a SIGNED amount supplied by the caller (`Fee { magnitude, negative }`). `settle_fee` validates only that `fee.magnitude <= MAX_FEE` — it never checks that the fee is non-negative. A fee is meant to be SUBTRACTED from the account's collateral, but the negative branch ADDS `magnitude` to collateral instead (`acct.collateral = acct.collateral + fee.magnitude`). So an attacker submits a fee with `negative = true` and a magnitude up to MAX_FEE, and instead of paying a fee their collateral is credited for free. Repeating this inflates their collateral without any deposit; they then `withdraw` the fabricated balance, draining real SUI from the shared exchange vault at the expense of other depositors. A fee input must be constrained to be non-negative (`assert!(!fee.negative)` / reject a signed fee below zero) before it is applied. This mirrors the real Aftermath perpetuals exploit where an unchecked negative signed fee turned `value - fee` into `value + |fee|`.
